basis: Inherited erythrocytosis defines disease; thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication despite its high annotated frequency.
Calcification of dental pulp; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Epidermal nevi and phosphate-wasting, vitamin D-resistant rickets define this cutaneous and skeletal metabolic syndrome.
Severe hypothyroidism with defining cerebral dysfunction, altered consciousness or coma; systemic slowing alone does not establish other organ damage.
AGXT, glyoxylate parent and hyperoxaluria child support renal oxalate injury in most; the definition's plasmalogen wording is inconsistent.
Cardiac and skeletal defects characterize Noonan syndrome; motor delay 9/12 and intellectual disability 2/5; persistent keratosis pilaris 4/9. Myopia 3/11 is below 30%.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow; the defining translocation does not establish another affected organ.
Craniosynostosis, maxillary skeletal retrusion and intellectual disability define syndrome; palatal shape alone does not establish gastrointestinal injury.
Persistent cutaneous hyperpigmentation and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis define disease.
Anomalous pulmonary venous drainage with shunting and characteristic lung hypoplasia define this cardiopulmonary malformation syndrome.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, hypotonia and movement abnormalities define disease; visual impairment in 3/5 is cerebral rather than intrinsic eye damage.
MAC causes infection; chronic pulmonary infection directly damages lungs in a substantial share (>30%). Nodal and disseminated forms do not imply uniform other-organ injury.
Defining oral and tongue malformations accompany mandibular and limb skeletal anomalies; additional organs vary across subtypes.
Neurocutaneous syndrome defined by epidermal nevi and associated developmental or epileptic abnormalities; reported eye findings lack qualifying frequency.
Congenital connective-tissue bands join the eyelids and restrict eye opening.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat, sometimes with epidermal atrophy; systemic metabolic dysfunction is not characteristic.
Disease is explicitly located in the facial nerve; additional manifestations are not shared across this umbrella.
Ear abnormalities and hearing impairment define branchiootic syndrome; lacrimal stenosis has unspecified frequency, and renal disease is not defining.
Viral hemorrhagic fever with thrombocytopenia and bleeding; hepatocellular injury occurs commonly (>30%). Neurologic complications affect a minority.
Anterior horn motor neuron disease; scapular and peroneal muscle wasting are defining manifestations, establishing substantial skeletal muscle loss.
Cerebellar and motor-system degeneration defines disease; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction, not intrinsic eye injury.
Inherited abnormal bone sclerosis; marrow failure and cranial nerve injury are not established across most patients in this umbrella.
Posture-dependent urinary protein loss is a renal condition; it does not establish progressive renal damage or another affected organ.
RP1-associated retinal degeneration; conflicting inheritance wording does not alter the retinal organ assignment.
Acid-base imbalance defines this metabolic axis condition; respiratory and renal causes do not establish shared lung or kidney damage across the umbrella.
